free_text: The 68-year-old male presents with an elevated PSA of 11.7 ng/mL and a PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right mid peripheral zone, with a prior biopsy showing Gleason 3+3. The clinical T stage is cT1c. The management assessment is active surveillance due to the need to review individual treatment benefit and patient preferences. The trade-off involves balancing the risk of progression against the potential side effects of active treatment.
